title: The Per-Worker Fee and Its Billing-Error Credit: Computation
content:
## The line concerned

Under the Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement, the billing-error credit computed here is the one owed on the per-worker fee line most recently billed on the agreement, that is, the employer-paid per-worker fee line with the latest billing month.

## The per-worker fee

The per-worker fee for a billing month is the tier's per-worker monthly fee under the employer-paid fee model multiplied by the enrolled active workers on that month's census. The per-worker fee is formed in one fixed order: the way the fee is worked out comes first, a multiplier comes next, and percentages taken off are added together and taken off the result once. It is rounded half up to the cent once, as the last step of its computation.

## The billing-error credit

The billing-error credit is the amount billed on the per-worker fee line above the per-worker fee, never more than what is still unpaid on that line, the line amount less the payments and credits pointing to it; no credit is booked when that amount is not above zero, and a line that already carries a billing-error credit receives no second one.

| Records of the line | Credit |
|---|---|
| billed above the fee, nothing paid or credited | the amount billed above the fee |
| billed above the fee, partly paid | the lesser of the amount billed above the fee and the unpaid amount |
| billed at or below the fee | none |
| already carries a billing-error credit | none |

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

On a Growth-tier program with a per-worker monthly fee of 4.50 and a census of 137 enrolled active workers, the per-worker fee is 4.50 multiplied by 137, that is 616.50. A line billed at 661.50 with nothing paid or credited carries a billing-error credit of 45.00; had the employer already paid 640.00 against it, the unpaid amount would be 21.50 and the credit 21.50. A line billed at 610.00 carries no credit.
